Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Technology Suggested vocabulary Computer, record, type, information, internet, e
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Technology Suggested vocabulary Computer, record, type, information, internet, e in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to pronounce words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: The learner’s interaction with digital devices with assistive technology is enhanced as they listen or watch recordings and respond to

them appropriately.

• Communication and collaboration: The learner’s ability to speak engagingly is developed as they use vocabulary related to technology in

communication.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively with peers during language games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is nurtured enhanced as they listen attentively and responds appropriately to instructions.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner uses the skill of correct pronunciation to learn similar concept in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

• Print textbooks in appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille books

• Digital devices with assistive technology,

• Charts, flash cards or braille cards,

• Pictures or picture description
